newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Gov't to mediate in Colombia port workers' strike.
newsitem.headline: Gov't to mediate in Colombia port workers' strike.

text.p: Labor Ministry officials were due to arrive in the Pacific port of Buenaventura Friday in a bid to negotiate an end to the three-day-old dock workers' strike that has paralyzed much of Colombia's export sector, local media reports said.

El Pais, the leading daily in the southwest city of Cali, said the Labor Ministry delegates would seek to mediate between Port Authority officials and cargo operators and representatives of the estimated 2,700 dock workers in Buenaventura, who voted to lay down tools late Tuesday to press for higher wages and sickness and injury benefits.

According to El Pais, the steamy streets of Buenaventura have been clogged with 1,500 tractor trailer trucks laden with sugar and other export items -- including perishable goods already beginning to rot -- since the strike began. More than 90,000 60- kg bags of coffee are among exports affected by the job action, according to the National Coffee Growers' Federation.

A preliminary accord aimed at ending the strike was reached early Thursday. But dock workers rejected the pact at a general assembly held later in the day, saying its promise of higher wages fell far short of their demands.
"There is no end in sight to this strike," a spokesman for Pan Servicios, a private customs agent, told Reuters late Thursday.
"We all thought everything was going to get back to normal this morning. And although we're hoping there's a quick solution, there's no way of knowing."
